Factory CEO Matan Grinberg said Wednesday that the AI coding startup has terminated Chris Degnan as a board observer and advisor, accusing him of allegedly violating confidentiality obligations by maintaining undisclosed, recurring conversations with rival Cognition.

The development comes as Degnan publicly announced that he is joining Cognition as its chief revenue officer, moving from an advisory role at Factory to an executive position at the company.

"I’m super excited to join Cognition as its Chief Revenue Officer," Degnan said in a post on X announcing the move. He described Cognition as another "rocket ship" and said customer feedback about Devin convinced him the opportunity was "once-in-a-lifetime."

Benzinga contacted Factory AI and Cognition for comment but did not receive a response at the time of publication. 

Grinberg, however, said in a post on X that Degnan had been advising Factory for more than a year and had access to confidential board-level information while also speaking with executives at Cognition, the company behind AI coding agent Devin.

"Yesterday, I made the decision to immediately terminate Christopher Degnan’s roles as a Board Observer and Advisor to Factory," Grinberg said

Read Also: OpenAI Targets $30 Billion Mega-Round After Putting IPO Plans on Hold

According to Grinberg, Degnan initially described his contact with a Cognition executive as a casual, one-off conversation; Grinberg later learned that the discussions were formal and recurring. Grinberg said Degnan advised Factory on confidential matters as recently as Monday, then told him that evening that the relationship with Cognition had been more extensive than previously disclosed.

"While he sat in our board meetings and advised our leadership team, he was also confiding with executives of our largest competitor," Grinberg wrote.

Grinberg did not specify what information Degnan may have shared with Cognition and said Factory does not know the extent of the disclosure.

He also pointed to questions Degnan had recently asked about Factory’s product roadmap and what Grinberg described as the company’s "parity gap" with competitors, saying those questions took on a different significance in light of the newly disclosed conversations.

Degnan did not directly address Grinberg’s allegations in his public announcement of joining Cognition.

Instead, he highlighted his previous experience helping build Snowflake’s sales organization and said he was excited to work with Cognition CEO Scott Wu, President Russell Kaplan, and the broader team.

"While I am not jumping on as the first sales rep this time, I can’t wait to dive in and help drive amazing customer outcomes while building a world-class sales team," Degnan wrote.

Degnan joined Factory as an advisor in November 2025 after more than a decade at Snowflake, where he was the company’s first sales hire and eventually became chief revenue officer. Snowflake announced his retirement from the CRO role in March 2025. 

At the time of his Factory appointment, the company described Degnan as bringing “extensive experience” in enterprise sales and scaling technology businesses.

In his post, Grinberg also accused Cognition engineers of posing as candidates during interviews with Factory in an effort to obtain information about the company’s products. He said Factory’s decision to cut ties with Degnan was ultimately about maintaining trust around its confidential information.

"Trust in Board Membership is one of the sacred bonds in Silicon Valley," Grinberg said. "With it comes an enormous responsibility. That trust was violated."

Shares of Summit Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ:SMMT) moved higher in Wednesday afternoon trading, extending gains from the previous session following a landmark $2 billion strategic equity investment from pharmaceutical titan AstraZeneca to accelerate the clinical development of ivonescimab.

Here’s what investors need to know.

  • Summit Therapeutics shares are climbing with conviction. What’s behind SMMT gains?

$2 Billion Strategic Equity Injection

Late Monday, Summit announced that AstraZeneca agreed to invest $2 billion in newly issued convertible preferred shares. At the conversion ratio, the investment equates to an implied common stock price of $18.36 per share.

The multi-billion-dollar capital commitment provides Summit with substantial balance sheet runway to advance ivonescimab, its investigational potential first-in-class bispecific antibody targeting PD-1 and VEGF. Closing of the preferred stock investment is expected within one week, subject to customary regulatory clearances.

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Strategic Oncology Clinical Collaboration

Alongside the equity financing, Summit entered into a co-funded clinical collaboration agreement with AstraZeneca to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with AstraZeneca’s sonesitatug vedotin (Sone-Ve), a Claudin 18.2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, in gastrointestinal cancers. Under the agreement, AstraZeneca will sponsor the combination studies while both companies retain full commercial and development rights to their respective molecules.

“This significant investment, as well as the collaboration, is a powerful validation of the potential of ivonescimab,” said Robert W. Duggan, Chairman and Co-Chief Executive Officer of Summit Therapeutics. “We are proud to welcome AstraZeneca as a strategic investor as we continue to work with purposeful urgency to make a significant difference for patients with cancer.”

Summit President and Co-CEO Dr. Maky Zanganeh added that the developments open “an exciting new chapter in the advancement of ivonescimab,” allowing the company to explore novel combination strategies alongside leading ADC assets.

SMMT Shares Climb Wednesday Afternoon

SMMT Price Action: Summit Therapeutics shares were up 5.74% at $17.32 at the time of publication on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Softer-than-expected U.S. inflation data triggered a notable rotation within technology stocks on Wednesday, with software and mega-cap technology ETFs outperforming semiconductor funds as investors scaled back expectations for another Federal Reserve rate hike.

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (BATS:IGV) gained around 2%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) slipped 0.2%, before gaining marginally. The broader Nasdaq Composite rose more than 1%, while the S&P 500 gained around 1%.

See More: Top Growth Stocks

Why Software Is Responding To The Inflation Data

The Commerce Department reported that August’s headline Personal Consumption Expenditures price index increased 3.4% year over year, below economists’ 3.7% forecast. Core PCE rose 3% annually. Markets subsequently reduced expectations for an October Fed hike.

That matters for growth-oriented stocks because their valuations depend heavily on expectations for earnings and cash flows further into the future. A less aggressive interest-rate outlook can therefore provide a valuation tailwind, particularly for software companies.

IGV provides concentrated exposure to this segment. The ETF tracks North American software companies along with select interactive media and services firms and had 106 holdings as of Sept. 24, with a 0.38% expense ratio. Its largest positions included Palo Alto Networks, Palantir Technologies Inc, CrowdStrike Holdings Inc, Microsoft Corp and Oracle Corp.

The software trade has also been gaining momentum. IGV rose about 38% in the past six months, as investors shifted attention toward companies translating AI adoption into software revenue and profits.

Why SOXX Lagged

SOXX offers a very different form of technology exposure. The ETF holds 30 semiconductor companies and had a 0.33% expense ratio. Its biggest holdings included Intel Corp, Advanced Micro Devices Inc, Micron Technology Inc, Nvidia Corp and Broadcom Inc, giving investors direct exposure to the AI-chip and semiconductor infrastructure cycle.

Wednesday’s divergence suggests that the softer inflation reading did not produce a uniform technology rally. Instead, investors appeared to favor software and mega-cap technology while semiconductor stocks lagged.

That makes the IGV-versus-SOXX performance gap worth watching. If expectations for Fed policy continue to ease, software could remain a key beneficiary, while semiconductor ETFs remain more closely tied to AI infrastructure spending, chip demand and earnings expectations.

Shares of defense company Boeing Co (NYSE:BA) traded higher on Tuesday after the company announced a new $20 billion contract from the U.S. government. That contract could help boost the share price and benefit the owners of BA stock, including several members of Congress.

Boeing Lands Pentagon Deal

Boeing was awarded a contract from the U.S. Navy for up to $20 billion to develop the next-generation fighter.

This marks the second major sixth-generation fighter win for Boeing and comes with the company beating out defense competitor Northrop Grumman Corp. (NYSE:NOC) for the contract. Boeing beat out Lockheed Martin for a $20 billion development contract for the Air Force’s F-47 last year.

The award covers multiple test aircraft and weapons-integration testing. Boeing securing the contract and tests going well could lead to hundreds of billions of dollars in the future, as reported by Reuters.

“F/A-XX will dominate contested airspace, extend operational reach, and deliver a decisive combat advantage for the warfighter,” Pentagon acquisition chief Michael Duffey said.

The next-generation aircraft is intended to replace the current F/A-18E/F Super Hornet and EA-18 G Growler in the 2030s.

Duffey called the future aircraft a "crucial, non-negotiable investment" for the U.S. Navy.

A decision on this contract faced multiple delays and saw Congress intervene. Lockheed Martin was eliminated from the competition previously with Boeing and Northrop the two finalists for the development deal.

Read Also: Congressman On Armed Services Committee Can't Stop Buying Defense Stock: 9 Purchases Since September

Congress Members Buy Boeing Stock

Congressional trading in defense stocks has drawn sustained criticism from ethics groups and fueled bipartisan proposals to bar members from trading individual stocks. Purchases made during periods of heightened geopolitical conflict attract particular scrutiny.

Congressional disclosures show three members reported buying Boeing stock earlier in 2026, before the award was announced. That Boeing and Northrop were the program’s two finalists had been publicly reported.

Under the STOCK Act, members report trades in value ranges rather than exact amounts, and disclosures also cover trades made by a spouse or by an advisor with discretion over the account.

The members of Congress who have bought Boeing stock in 2026 are:

  • March 27: Sen. Alan Armstrong (R-Okla.), $1,000 to $15,000
  • March 19: Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-Fla.), $16,000 to $65,000
  • Feb. 2: Rep. Julia Letlow (R-La.), $1,000 to $15,000

Several other members have sold Boeing stock this year, and several likely own Boeing stock purchased before the start of 2026.

Boeing Stock Rises

On Wednesday, Boeing stock was down 0.96% to $185.88. The stock is down 13.6% year-to-date and several members who have bought stock are likely down on their initial purchase this year.

Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU) reported financial results for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 after the closing bell on Wednesday. Here’s a look at the key details from the print.

  • Micron Technology stock is trending. What’s next for MU stock?

Micron Q4 Highlights

Micron posted fourth-quarter revenue of $54.23 billion, beating analyst estimates of $50.75 billion, according to Benzinga Pro. The semiconductor company reported adjusted earnings of $33.42 per share, beating estimates of $31.45 per share.

Total revenue was up approximately 379% on a year-over-year basis. Operating cash flow came in at $43.97 billion versus $25.39 billion in the prior quarter and $5.73 billion in the comparable quarter last year. The company generated $33.20 billion of adjusted free cash flow in the fourth quarter.

Micron reported $10.77 billion of capital expenditures and ended the quarter with $73.48 billion in cash, marketable investments and restricted cash.

“Micron delivered record fiscal 2026 results, and we expect an even stronger fiscal 2027,” said Sanjay Mehrotra, chairman, president and CEO of Micron.

Micron expects first-quarter revenue of $60 billion to $63 billion versus estimates of $56.55 billion. The company anticipates first-quarter adjusted earnings of $37.15 to $39.15 per share, versus estimates of $35.07 per share.

“AI is becoming Super Intelligence (SI), and memory enhances this intelligence and the competitiveness of our customers’ platforms. We are increasing our investments in technology, products and manufacturing to help drive SI forward with our customers, and our Strategic Customer Agreements provide added confidence in the durability of Micron’s financial performance,” Mehrotra said.

Micron’s board declared a quarterly dividend of 15 cents per share, payable on Oct. 29 to shareholders of record as of Oct. 14.

Management will discuss the quarter on an earnings call with investors and analysts at 4:30 p.m. ET.

Bain Capital is weighing a more than $15 billion purchase of Koch-owned data-center operator Edged, marking a potential major shift for the private equity firm as it moves deeper into the booming U.S. AI infrastructure market.

According to Bloomberg, the firm held discussions regarding the potential acquisition of Edged to develop, build and operate data centers. Edge currently operates seven data centers, with more additional projects on the way.

Koch Inc. hired Goldman Sachs and Newmark Group to gauge interest from potential buyers.

Read Also: OpenAI, Anthropic Face New FTC Probe Over AI Agent Risks

Bain managing partner David Gross warned late last year in an interview that the surge of investment into AI infrastructure could be creating "a massive arms race," signaling concerns about the sheer amount of capital pouring into the sector.

FMI Consulting recently identified seven data center service sectors as potential private equity acquisition targets. The areas include electrical and mechanical contractors, operations and maintenance providers, equipment distributors, engineering firms, and data center infrastructure specialists. 

U.S. data center construction spending jumped from $9.9 billion in 2021 to $49.7 billion in 2025. FMI expects spending to reach $100.8 billion by 2030, with roughly $397 billion in cumulative construction spending over the next five years.

Last April, Bain Capital announced the launch of hyperscale provider scale, as the firm expanded its digital infrastructure footprint across the EMEA region.

Bain has also invested in data center developer Crusoe and operator DC Blox through its credit arm, with much of its broader data center focus centered on Europe and Asia. 

In the U.S., the firm has instead targeted companies that help data centers operate more efficiently. Its investments include cloud software and infrastructure company Nutanix and Coherent Corp., a supplier of data center components.
